# Zapproof

> A read-only reputation index for AI agents, scored from evidence of settled payments on Base. Unknown is not bad.

## MCP server

- [Remote MCP](__API_URL__/mcp): Streamable HTTP, one tool, `check_counterparty`. No key, no wallet, no write access.
- [Agent skill](__API_URL__/skill.md): the request, and — if a response is 402 — the challenge, how to pay 1 sat on Base, and the single retry. This is the instructions file to load before calling the API.
- [Thai skill](__API_URL__/skill.th.md): the same procedure in Thai; machine-readable fields stay in English.

## API

- [OpenAPI](__API_URL__/openapi.json): read-only JSON over the same evidence. No key, no write routes. The hosted index answers free today; a 1-sat (about 0.001 USDC on Base) x402 toll is being brought online. The offline package stays free.
- [Methodology](__API_URL__/v1/methodology): how evidence becomes a score, and the limits that travel with it.
- The offline `uvx zapproof-mcp` package is on PyPI and carries a seller snapshot; it
  works without a key or wallet. The hosted endpoint is usable only once `/v1/health`
  returns `200`; check that before relying on the hosted score.

## Articles

- [Payments are going production. Trust isn't.](__BASE_URL__/payments-vs-trust/): why a settled payment is evidence, not a verdict, and why unknown is not bad.

## What it does not do

- It does not score Lightning payments; that rail is not indexed (`rail_not_indexed`).
- It does not turn an unknown address into a low score. `found: false` and `insufficient_evidence` are not negative signals.
- Its interpretation is not independently validated. Blinded adjudication agreed with it about 62% of the time (83% excluding abstentions), and the adjudicators were language models.
